title: The Little Raccoon and Baby's First Halloween
summary: On Baby's very first Halloween, a little raccoon big brother in a firefighter costume guides the way door to door, remembering please and thank you, waiting patiently, taking turns and sharing a treat Baby can eat, then heads home proud, loved and sleepy.
character: the little raccoon, a small young raccoon with soft silver-grey fur, a black mask stripe across big round friendly eyes, a cream-white muzzle, small rounded ears, and a bushy tail with black and grey rings, wearing a bright red firefighter coat with yellow stripes and a small shiny red firefighter helmet

pages.text: On Halloween evening, a little raccoon zipped up his bright red firefighter coat and buckled on his shiny red helmet. "I'm ready to trick-or-treat!" he announced. From the hallway came a tiny squeal: "Ba-ba-BOO!" It was Baby, dressed as a round orange pumpkin, wiggling in the little red wagon. It was Baby's very first Halloween.

pages.text: Mama Raccoon smiled. "Raccoons are lucky," she said. "We already wear masks!" The little raccoon giggled and touched the black stripe across his eyes. Then Papa Raccoon knelt down. "Big brother, will you be Baby's guide tonight?" The little raccoon stood up very tall. "I will!"

pages.text: Outside, the moon was round and the street glowed with friendly jack-o'-lanterns. The little raccoon wanted to zoom from house to house like a speedy fire truck. But Baby's wagon went bumpity-bump, slow and steady. So he took a deep breath and walked right beside it, step by step. "We're a team," he whispered.

pages.text: At the first door, a cheerful badger in a witch costume held out a bowl of candy. The little raccoon remembered his manners. "Trick or treat, please!" he said. Baby just stared with big round eyes. "Now we say thank you," he explained gently. "Thank you!" he said, and Baby clapped two tiny paws. Clap, clap!

pages.text: At the next house, an old turtle opened the door very, very slowly. Creak. The little raccoon wanted to knock again, but he waited patiently, tapping his boots. "Good things come to those who wait," Papa murmured. When the turtle finally appeared, she gave them each a shiny red apple and a friendly wink.

pages.text: Then they reached a house where a crowd of costumed friends waited on the steps: a bunny astronaut, a fox pirate, and a hedgehog dressed as a dragon. Everyone wanted to go first! The little raccoon stepped aside. "You can go before us," he offered. "Taking turns is fair." The hedgehog grinned. "Next time, you go first!"

pages.text: Baby's turn came at last. Baby reached into the big bowl, grabbed one candy, and dropped it. Plop! Baby grabbed another. Plop! The little raccoon laughed. "Silly Baby, the candy goes in the bucket, not on the doormat!" He helped Baby's tiny paw find the pumpkin bucket. Plink! Everyone cheered.

pages.text: Soon the little raccoon's bucket was heavy and full. But when he peeked into Baby's bucket, he frowned. "Baby can't eat chewy candy or crunchy lollipops yet," he said. "Baby doesn't have enough teeth!" Mama nodded. "What could Baby enjoy instead?" The little raccoon thought and thought.

pages.text: Then he remembered the soft, sweet banana tucked in his pocket for a snack. "Baby, this is for you!" He peeled it carefully and broke off a tiny piece. Baby munched and smacked and squealed with delight. A soft banana was the very best treat of all.

pages.text: On the way home, Mama and Papa kept cooing over Baby. "Look at those chubby cheeks!" For a moment, the little raccoon felt invisible, like a ghost. He kicked a crunchy leaf. Then Papa gave him a big hug. "And look at our brave firefighter, the best big brother in the whole neighborhood!"

pages.text: Soon Baby yawned a huge, wobbly yawn. "I think Baby is sleepy," said the little raccoon. "May I pull the wagon the rest of the way?" Mama smiled. "That would be very helpful, thank you." So he pulled, gently and slowly, past the glowing pumpkins, all the way home.

pages.text: At home, everyone traded costumes for cozy pajamas. The little raccoon counted his candy, one, two, three, all the way to twenty. Baby snuggled in Mama's lap and nibbled the last bit of banana. "Did Baby like Halloween?" he asked. Baby gave him a sticky, sleepy smile. That meant yes.

pages.text: At bedtime, Papa tucked the little raccoon under his blanket. "You were gentle, patient, and kind tonight," Papa whispered. "We are so proud of you." The little raccoon felt warm all the way to the tip of his striped tail. Across the room, Baby was already dreaming. "Happy first Halloween, Baby," he whispered, and closed his eyes.
